sections.heading: License responsibilities, points and sanctions
sections.markdown:
## C2 — License responsibilities, points and sanctions

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A27
For a citation dated November 14, 2020 or later, driving 1 through 5 miles per hour above the limit adds no points inside or outside city limits. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A27
Inside city limits, speeding more than 5 but no more than 10 miles per hour above the limit carries 2 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A27
Inside city limits, speeding more than 10 through 35 miles per hour above the limit carries 3 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A27
Speeding more than 35 miles per hour above the limit carries 4 points inside or outside city limits. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A27
Outside city limits, speeding more than 5 through 10 miles per hour above the limit carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A27
Outside city limits, speeding more than 10 through 15 miles per hour above the limit carries 2 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A27
Outside city limits, speeding more than 15 through 35 miles per hour above the limit carries 3 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A27
Driving with an expired license or without ever having received a license carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A27
A provisional or school permit passenger violation carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A27
A wireless-device violation under provisional, learner, school or school learner permit restrictions carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A27
A traffic conviction adds points using the violation date rather than the conviction date. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A27
Traffic convictions stay on the driving record for 5 years. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A27
Points stop counting 2 years after the violation date. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A27
An out-of-state traffic conviction receives Nebraska points as though the violation happened in Nebraska. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A27
A driver without a CDL or CLP may receive a two-point credit after successfully completing a DMV-approved improvement course before the violation that would bring the total to twelve points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A27
The improvement-course point credit can be used only once every 5 years. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A28
A serious traffic conviction can result in a court-ordered license revocation for the period the court specifies. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A28
Court-ordered revocation requires financial-responsibility proof for 3 years after the original revocation’s ending date. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A28
The court returns an impounded license when the impoundment period ends. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A28
Driving during general court-ordered impoundment brings a one-year revocation upon conviction, while driving during the separately stated underage drinking or refusal impoundment brings six months. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A28
For a driver aged 20 or younger, a conviction under the alcohol-content rule of 0.02 percent leads to 30 days of court impoundment. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A28
For a driver aged twenty or younger, the conviction under the 0.02-percent alcohol rule remains on the record for ninety days and is then deleted. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A28
An underage refusal conviction leads to 90 days of court impoundment. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R24 | anchor: A28
An underage refusal conviction remains on the record for 120 days and is then deleted. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R25 | anchor: A28
A driver convicted of driving during impoundment under the underage drinking or refusal procedure receives a six-month court-ordered license revocation. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R26 | anchor: A28
Administrative revocation permits immediate license confiscation after an alcohol-test failure or refusal of an alcohol-or-drug chemical test. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R27 | anchor: A28
A first alcohol-test failure brings a 180-day administrative revocation. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R28 | anchor: A28
A later alcohol-test failure brings a year of administrative revocation. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R29 | anchor: A28
Refusing a chemical alcohol-or-drug test brings a year of administrative revocation. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R30 | anchor: A28
A driver subject to administrative revocation may request a hearing to challenge it. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R31 | anchor: A28
A driver who requests an administrative-revocation hearing cannot drive with an interlock or sobriety permit until the court orders it as part of sentencing. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R32 | anchor: A29
Waiving the administrative hearing can allow eligible driving with an ignition-interlock permit during some or all of the revocation. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R33 | anchor: A29
A participant in the 24/7 sobriety program who has a court-certified order must obtain a Sobriety Program Permit. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R34 | anchor: A29
A sobriety program permit permits driving during administrative revocation only when the driving record otherwise allows it. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R35 | anchor: A29
For a subsequent offense, sobriety-permit eligibility begins 45 days after the temporary license expires. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R36 | anchor: A29
After chemical-test refusal, sobriety-permit eligibility begins 90 days after the temporary license expires. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R37 | anchor: A29
A sobriety program permit is revoked when the DMV receives a conviction abstract revoking driving privileges or a court order revoking that permit. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R38 | anchor: A29
A sobriety-permit participant must be at least 18 and have held or tested for a Class O or Class M license. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R39 | anchor: A29
A sobriety program permit does not authorize commercial vehicle operation. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R40 | anchor: A29
An employment drive permit after qualifying point or child-support revocation allows only direct home-and-work travel under its employment terms. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R41 | anchor: A29
An employment drive permit does not authorize commercial vehicle operation. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R42 | anchor: A29
An eligible first-time administrative-revocation offender may apply for an interlock permit after the temporary license’s 15 days expire. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R43 | anchor: A29
For a first-time offender subject to administrative license revocation, the interlock permit lasts six months and allows driving a vehicle equipped with the interlock system. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R44 | anchor: A29
For a later administrative-revocation offense, interlock-permit eligibility begins 45 days after temporary-license expiration. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R45 | anchor: A30
After chemical-test refusal, interlock-permit eligibility begins 90 days after temporary-license expiration. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R46 | anchor: A30
A court or the Board of Pardons may order interlock use for as long as 15 years, depending on the record and prior convictions. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R47 | anchor: A30
The base offense for a driver’s interlock tampering, circumvention or driving without the required device is a Class I misdemeanor. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R48 | anchor: A30
The handbook describes an alcohol-related Class IV felony enhancement for a driver’s interlock tampering, circumvention or driving without the required device, but does not specify the alcohol-threshold unit. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R49 | anchor: A30
Interlock-permit eligibility requires having held a Class O or Class M license. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R50 | anchor: A30
After point revocation, a medical-hardship permit limits travel to trips from home or work to the specified treatment location and back. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R51 | anchor: A30
Fleeing to avoid arrest for a felony is a Class IV felony and can also cause license revocation. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R52 | anchor: A30
A conviction for leaving a motor-vehicle crash scene can revoke the driver license for as long as a year. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R53 | anchor: A30
For a driver aged 20 or younger, a first minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for 30 days. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R54 | anchor: A30
For a person aged twenty or younger, a second minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for ninety days. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R55 | anchor: A30
For a person aged twenty or younger, a third or later minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for twelve months. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R56 | anchor: A30
An unlicensed person aged twenty or younger cannot obtain a permit or license for thirty days after a first minor-in-possession conviction, ninety days after a second, or twelve months after a third or later conviction. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R57 | anchor: A31
For a juvenile aged 17 or younger, a first juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for 30 days. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R58 | anchor: A31
For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, a second juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for ninety days. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R59 | anchor: A31
For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, a third or later juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for twelve months. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R60 | anchor: A31
An unlicensed juvenile aged seventeen or younger cannot obtain a permit or license for thirty days after a first juvenile-court drug conviction, ninety days after a second, or twelve months after a third or later conviction. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R61 | anchor: A31
For any juvenile-court offense involving a person aged 17 or younger, the court may impound driving documents for 30 days. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-R62 | anchor: A31
A driver whose license was suspended, revoked, cancelled or disqualified must complete reinstatement before a new license can be issued. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> pdf-0031]

verification_debt.claim_text: Edition and revision frequency are unconfirmed under registrar location policy; the printed date is outside permitted observation pages.

Fact sec03-R48 preserves the supported interlock enhancement while withholding the original unitless alcohol-content threshold. The cited physical page thirty prints the magnitude without a unit. Official source evidence resolving the unit is required; no percent, BAC unit or operative numeric threshold is asserted.
